title: The filter chrome exposes accessible controls and refetches every tile with the same boundary
asA: operator narrowing the dashboard with a filter chip or a filter input
iWant: the filter chrome to expose accessible controls that carry the operator's choice to every fetch and refetch every tile with the same boundary
soThat: the shell renders a filtered view at one boundary without drifting between tiles

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered dashboard surface with filter chrome, every filter control (chip, dropdown, search input) is a labelled interactive element (a `<button>`, a `<select>` or an `<input>`) with an accessible name; the controls are keyboard-reachable in reading order before the tile row; the operator's active filter selection is reflected on the shell as a `data-active-filters` attribute the pack can read. A filter chrome that ships hover-only controls (a hover-reveal menu on a mouseover element) fails project-side review.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered dashboard with filter chrome
acceptanceCriteria.then: every filter control is a labelled interactive element keyboard-reachable in reading order

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given an operator-driven filter change (activate a filter chip, type into a filter input), the shell issues one refetch per tile and one per rendered chart with the same `filter` query parameter set applied to every fetch; the shell's `data-active-filters` attribute updates on the same paint as the refetch batch. This AC is a runtime-observable fan-out clause; the pack asserts the fetch fan-out on the timeframe seam (AC-19104-1) which the fixture drives; the filter fan-out is a mechanism-reach gap the README names for a v1.1 minor bump.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered dashboard and a filter change
acceptanceCriteria.then: every refetch carries the same active-filters set and the shell attribute updates
